description: A library for asp.net core that allows you to send emails without having memory leaks
releaseNotes:
2.4.0: Optional concurrent sends. The new MaxConcurrentSends option (configuration key of the same name, default 1 = the 2.3.0 behaviour exactly, capped at 16) lets one worker send up to N emails at the same time, each sender with its own database context and its own SMTP connection. Priority, per-partition turns, the CAS claim, the retry budget, the stale-claim reclaim and the per-email send timeout are unchanged; the probe after an outage pause is always sent alone, and no new send starts once a pause is declared or the host is stopping. No schema change. A host that registers its own ISender must make it thread safe before raising the option.
2.3.0: Priority and per-partition fairness (new Priority and PartitionKey columns, new EnqueueAsync overload taking EmailEnqueueOptions); the failure reason is recorded on the row (new LastError and LastErrorOn columns); retry waits can be capped (MaxRetryBackoffSeconds) and can no longer overflow into an immediate-retry loop; optional outage pause (OutagePauseThreshold) so a mail server outage does not burn every queued email's retry budget; periodic wake (PollIntervalSeconds, default 120) so rows made due outside the process are picked up; the worker can no longer wedge after an exception or run two loops at once; stale claims count as a failed attempt; StaleClaimMinutes is bindable from configuration. A send that hangs no longer holds the queue: every send is bounded by the new SendTimeoutSeconds option (default 60, connect and TLS included); past it the connection is aborted, the attempt is recorded (TimeoutException in LastError) and retried after its backoff, and the worker goes on with the next email. The worker no longer sends through FluentEmail.Smtp's SmtpSender, which ignores cancellation, nor through one SmtpClient for the life of the process, whose idle connection was reused and, once dropped silently by a NAT, hung about 16 minutes: one connection per pass, reused only while sends are under 30 seconds apart (at most 50 messages), closed with QUIT at the end of the pass. The message built is the same. SCHEMA CHANGE: the host must add four columns to the queue table, see the README section "Upgrading to 2.3.0". (Includes 2.3.0-rc.1 and 2.3.0-rc.2.)
2.2.1: Fix stale-claim reclaim missing legacy rows — rows moved to Sending by pre-2.2.0 code have no NextAttemptOn deadline stamped and were orphaned forever; the reclaim now also recovers NULL-deadline Sending rows older than StaleClaimMinutes (by CreatedOn) back to Error for normal retry. No schema change.
2.2.0: Atomic CAS claim of queued emails (ExecuteUpdateAsync Pending/Error -> Sending only if the row is still in the read status) so multiple worker instances can no longer double-send; stale-claim reclaim of rows left in Sending past a stamped deadline (reuses the existing NextAttemptOn column, no schema change); new RunHostedService option to gate the background worker on parked/standby instances while keeping EnqueueAsync available; configurable StaleClaimMinutes (default 10).
